experiment_description: CMS/LHC proton-proton collision data at center-of-mass energy sqrt(s)=13 TeV were used to characterize the spin quantum state of top-quark--antiquark (t tbar) pairs in the lepton+jets decay channel. The input measurement was the doubly differential extraction of the t tbar spin density matrix in bins of invariant mass m(t tbar) and absolute top production angle |cos(theta)|, where theta is the top-quark production angle in the t tbar center-of-mass frame relative to the proton beam direction. The analyzed phase-space bins were m(t tbar) in [300,400], [400,600], [600,800], and [800,13000] GeV, crossed with |cos(theta)| in [0.0,0.4], [0.4,0.7], and [0.7,1.0]. In each bin, the top and antitop spin state was reconstructed as a two-qubit density matrix rho_t_tbar = (1/4)(I2 tensor I2 + sum_i P_i sigma_i tensor I2 + sum_j Pbar_j I2 tensor sigma_j + sum_ij C_ij sigma_i tensor sigma_j), where I2 is the 2 by 2 identity, sigma_i are Pauli matrices, P_i and Pbar_j are the top and antitop polarization components, and C_ij is the spin-correlation matrix. The spin analyzers were charged leptons and d-type quarks from top decays. This record uses the helicity basis, an event-dependent right-handed basis in the t tbar center-of-mass frame defined by unit vectors (khat, nhat, rhat), with khat along the top-quark flight direction, rhat=(phat - cos(theta) khat)/sin(theta), nhat=rhat cross khat, and the sign convention nhat -> sgn(cos(theta)) nhat and rhat -> sgn(cos(theta)) rhat. Because the helicity-basis orientation changes event by event, observables integrated over phase space characterize event-dependent, so-called fictitious, two-qubit spin states rather than a fixed-laboratory-axis spin state. From the fitted polarization and spin-correlation coefficients, the following dimensionless quantum-information observables were computed per bin. The top-quark quantum discord D_t is measured in bits using log base 2 and is D_t = S(rho_tbar) - S(rho_t_tbar) + min_uhat[p_{+uhat} S(rho_{t,+uhat}) + p_{-uhat} S(rho_{t,-uhat})], where S(rho)=-Tr(rho log2 rho), rho_t=Tr_tbar(rho_t_tbar), rho_tbar=Tr_t(rho_t_tbar), Pi_{±uhat} are projectors for a spin measurement of the antitop along unit vector uhat, p_{±uhat}=Tr[(I2 tensor Pi_{±uhat}) rho_t_tbar (I2 tensor Pi_{±uhat})], and rho_{t,±uhat}=Tr_tbar[(I2 tensor Pi_{±uhat}) rho_t_tbar (I2 tensor Pi_{±uhat})]/p_{±uhat}; the minimization over uhat was numerical. The entanglement marker Delta_E is the Peres-Horodecki-based marker used for the same reconstructed spin state, with the separability boundary Delta_E=1 and Delta_E>1 denoting entanglement. The steering marker T is T = integral d^2 uhat sqrt(uhat^T C^T C uhat), with the steering threshold T=2*pi for the unpolarized two-qubit criterion. The Bell-correlation marker B is B=m1+m2, where m1 and m2 are the two largest eigenvalues of C^T C; B>1 is the CHSH Bell-correlation threshold for the reconstructed state. The mixed-state magic observable M2_tilde is the second-stabilizer-Renyi-entropy-based quantity M2_tilde = -log2((1 + sum_i(P_i^4 + Pbar_i^4) + sum_ij C_ij^4)/(1 + sum_i(P_i^2 + Pbar_i^2) + sum_ij C_ij^2)). Central values were obtained by minimizing the negative log-likelihood -2 log L = sum_ij (o_i-x_i) U^{-1}_{ij} (o_j-x_j), where o_i are measured polarization/spin-correlation coefficients, U_ij is their covariance matrix, and x_i are fitted coefficients constrained to the physical interval [-1,1].
